function.mechanism: Hydrophilic cellulose ether that binds water, increases viscosity, and forms gels that stabilize food structure and emulsions.

adi.basis: EFSA (2018, celluloses group E460-E469) concluded no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses and use levels.

efsa.key_finding: For unmodified/modified celluloses including E461, EFSA found low acute toxicity, no genotoxic concern, no carcinogenic signal in available studies, and no safety concern at reported use levels.

fda.notes: USP methylcellulose with methoxy content 27.5%-31.5% (dry weight); generally recognized as safe when used per good manufacturing practice.

adi.basis: WHO JECFA database entry for methyl cellulose (INS 461) lists ADI as NOT SPECIFIED (group ADI for modified celluloses).

concerns.summary: Recent human/food-fiber evidence indicates methylcellulose can alter fermentation dynamics and gas-related GI responses; this reflects tolerance/mechanistic effects rather than established systemic toxicity.
Direct modern additive-specific long-term epidemiology for E461 is limited; EFSA relied on a broad celluloses dataset with read-across across related cellulose derivatives.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2018 concluded no need for a numerical ADI and no safety concern at reported uses/use levels for celluloses including E461.
JECFA lists methyl cellulose under a NOT SPECIFIED group ADI for modified celluloses.
eCFR lists methylcellulose in 21 CFR 182.1480 as GRAS under GMP conditions.

adi_exceedance.notes: No numerical ADI is set by EFSA/JECFA for this celluloses group; EFSA reported no safety concern at assessed exposures.

risk_assessment.rationale: Convergent regulatory conclusions (EFSA no numerical ADI/no concern, FDA GRAS status with GMP, JECFA ADI not specified) support low toxicological concern at food-use levels; remaining uncertainty is mostly about GI tolerance and limited additive-specific modern epidemiology rather than severe hazard.
key_factors: EFSA 2018 re-evaluation for E460-E469 including E461: no safety concern at reported uses
FDA/eCFR GRAS listing in 21 CFR 182.1480 with product specification and GMP condition
JECFA ADI not specified for modified celluloses including methyl cellulose
No IARC monograph classification identified for methyl cellulose
